world.title: Oman rescues 25 from burning tanker as Iran halts ships
world.summary: Omani naval forces rescued 25 crew members from the Panamanian-flagged ship RITI after an attack sparked a fire near Oman on Oct. 30, the country’s Maritime Security Centre said. The crew received medical care. Oman did not identify who carried out the attack. Ship-tracking service MarineTraffic identified RITI as a cr
world.content: Omani naval forces rescued 25 crew members from the Panamanian-flagged ship RITI after an attack sparked a fire near Oman on Oct. 30, the country’s Maritime Security Centre said. The crew received medical care. Oman did not identify who carried out the attack. Ship-tracking service MarineTraffic identified RITI as a crude-oil tanker. Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said it halted oil tankers after incidents or mine strikes, blaming vessels that used routes Tehran considers unauthorized. The United States said it had cleared the strait’s recognized main transit routes of Iranian mines, while its counterblockade of Iranian ports remains in force. The waterway normally carries about one-fifth of global oil, and shipping traffic there is about 70% below prewar levels, according to the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency. A Qatari delegation also arrived in Tehran on Friday for talks with Iranian officials as mediators seek to revive talks with Washington.

world.title: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US election
world.summary: Pope Leo XIV cast a mail-in ballot in the U.S. midterm election, becoming the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election, the Vatican said Friday. The Chicago-born pontiff submitted the ballot in Chicago as a U.S. citizen; the Holy See did not disclose which candidates he selected. The Nov. 3 election will decide co
world.content: Pope Leo XIV cast a mail-in ballot in the U.S. midterm election, becoming the first pope to vote in a U.S. general election, the Vatican said Friday. The Chicago-born pontiff submitted the ballot in Chicago as a U.S. citizen; the Holy See did not disclose which candidates he selected. The Nov. 3 election will decide control of Congress: all 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are on the ballot, along with gubernatorial and local races. In Illinois, Leo’s ballot includes the governor’s race and the race for an open Senate seat following Sen. Dick Durbin’s retirement. Leo also holds Peruvian citizenship, and the Vatican said he voted whenever eligible while living in Peru. His U.S. vote follows public disputes with President Donald Trump over the Iran war and immigration enforcement; Leo has said he would continue speaking out against war and for peace. The midterms take place Tuesday, Nov. 3.
world.image_alt: Pope Leo becomes first pontiff to vote in US election

world.title: Italy
world.summary: Students, workers and other demonstrators joined a 24-hour general strike across dozens of Italian cities on Friday, Oct. 30, demanding higher wages, more funding for schools and public services, and relief from rising living costs. The grassroots trade union Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) estimated that 1 million to 1
world.content: Students, workers and other demonstrators joined a 24-hour general strike across dozens of Italian cities on Friday, Oct. 30, demanding higher wages, more funding for schools and public services, and relief from rising living costs. The grassroots trade union Unione Sindacale di Base (USB) estimated that 1 million to 1.5 million people took part; Italian authorities did not release an official count. Truck drivers, taxi drivers and farmers also protested fuel prices, while many marchers opposed higher military spending. Most demonstrations remained peaceful, but police used water cannon in Turin and Rome. Eight people were detained after repeatedly trying to break through police barricades during an attempt to march toward parliament, Japanese news agency ANSA reported. In Genoa, dockworkers and demonstrators protested the use of ports to ship weapons. The government has approved €175.2 million in fuel-cost assistance for truck drivers, farmers and fishermen. A proposed 2027 budget, still under discussion, includes an annual €2,500 bonus for workers under 30. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said Wednesday the measures were intended to address young people’s concerns, not to benefit those who vandalize property.

world.title: Brazil seeks answers after Senator Bolsonaro flees to US via Argentina
world.summary: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro said Friday that he fled to the United States because he was being “persecuted,” after losing the Oct. 25 presidential runoff to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and learning that police would revoke his passports as part of a money-laundering investigation. He secretly left Brazil
world.content: Brazilian Senator Flávio Bolsonaro said Friday that he fled to the United States because he was being “persecuted,” after losing the Oct. 25 presidential runoff to incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and learning that police would revoke his passports as part of a money-laundering investigation. He secretly left Brazil on Oct. 27, travelled through Argentina and Ecuador, and reached Florida the next day on a private jet. A Brazilian court had ordered him to surrender his passports and remain in the country during the investigation. In an Instagram livestream, Bolsonaro accused Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes of making false accusations and suggested election irregularities without citing specific evidence. He said he could seek the presidency before the next scheduled election in 2030. Brazil says it summoned Argentina’s chargé d’affaires on Oct. 29 to discuss his passage through the country, but Argentine Foreign Minister Pablo Quirno denied that Buenos Aires had received a request for explanations. The head of the airline that carried Bolsonaro said a U.S.-based broker hired the company but did not identify whom the broker represented. U.S. Democratic lawmakers have asked Secretary of State Marco Rubio to account for any government role, while the White House has not commented on the charter flight.
world.image_alt: Brazil seeks answers after Senator Bolsonaro flees to US via Argentina

world.title: Israel’s opposition weighs Arab-party backing as coalition talks begin
world.summary: Israeli party leaders are weighing coalition options after an election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc short of a majority. Arab-led parties could determine whether the opposition can replace him. The final count gave Netanyahu’s bloc 53 seats, opposition parties led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot
world.content: Israeli party leaders are weighing coalition options after an election left Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc short of a majority. Arab-led parties could determine whether the opposition can replace him. The final count gave Netanyahu’s bloc 53 seats, opposition parties led by former military chief Gadi Eisenkot 48, and Arab-led lists 19 in Israel’s 120-seat parliament, the Knesset. The opposition could reach 67 seats with Arab-party support, but Eisenkot and several allies ruled out cooperation during the campaign. Arab lawmakers have signaled a willingness to help remove Netanyahu. Joint List leader Yousef Jabareen said the party could support the opposition without joining its government. A unity government with Netanyahu is another option, though it would require leaders to reverse campaign pledges. After election officials formally submit the results on Nov. 4, President Isaac Herzog will consult party leaders and choose the candidate he considers most likely to form a government. The candidate has 28 days, with a possible 14-day extension; the new Knesset is due to convene Nov. 10.
world.image_alt: Israel’s opposition weighs Arab-party backing as coalition talks begin

world.title: Oleshky evacuation moves hundreds out as local ceasefire nears end
world.summary: Hundreds of residents left Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday as Russian and Ukrainian officials completed a joint evacuation and aid operation under a local truce, the first such mission since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion. The ceasefire, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and supported by Pope
world.content: Hundreds of residents left Russian-occupied Oleshky on Friday as Russian and Ukrainian officials completed a joint evacuation and aid operation under a local truce, the first such mission since Russia’s 2022 full-scale invasion. The ceasefire, brokered with help from U.S. first lady Melania Trump and supported by Pope Leo XIV, allowed food and medical supplies into the frontline town; officials have not confirmed the total number evacuated. People headed for Ukrainian-controlled areas were taken first to Anapa in southern Russia and were then due to fly to Belarus and travel by bus into Ukraine. The circuitous route avoids mined roads along the front line. More than 1,000 residents, many elderly, remained in the town, according to a report from the scene; they received food, medicine, hygiene supplies and fuel. The truce is due to end late Sunday, Nov. 1. The Russian and Ukrainian human rights commissioners have asked Melania Trump to help coordinate recurring relief missions, while peace talks involving Russia, Ukraine and the United States are expected to resume in Abu Dhabi in early November.
world.image_alt: Oleshky evacuation moves hundreds out as local ceasefire nears end

world.title: G20 talks end without consensus after Lavrov photo boycott
world.summary: The United States canceled the Group of 20 foreign ministers’ traditional opening photo in Atlanta on Friday, Oct. 30, after European delegates, including officials from the United Kingdom and Germany, objected to posing with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to walk out. U.S. Secretary of State Mar
world.content: The United States canceled the Group of 20 foreign ministers’ traditional opening photo in Atlanta on Friday, Oct. 30, after European delegates, including officials from the United Kingdom and Germany, objected to posing with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and threatened to walk out. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio scrapped the ceremony to keep it from becoming a distraction, U.S. officials said. The talks continued as planned. German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul said ministers should discuss disputes at the table but avoid images suggesting normal relations with Moscow. The two-day meeting ended Saturday without agreement on several major issues, including Russia’s war in Ukraine, the war involving the United States, Israel and Iran, and U.S. tariffs. Instead of a joint communiqué, Rubio was to issue a chair’s statement summarizing the discussions. The Atlanta meeting was intended to prepare for the G20 leaders’ summit in Miami on Dec. 14-15, hosted by President Donald Trump. Russian President Vladimir Putin has been invited, but the Kremlin has not confirmed whether he will attend. Russia, Ukraine and the United States were also expected to hold fresh negotiations in November.
world.image_alt: G20 talks end without consensus after Lavrov photo boycott

world.title: Russia
world.summary: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s last independent newspapers still operating inside the country, says it will end operations on Nov. 9 after losing access to its Moscow office and reader-donation system. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said Russian authorities and security services had forced the newsroom to stop working.
world.content: Novaya Gazeta, one of Russia’s last independent newspapers still operating inside the country, says it will end operations on Nov. 9 after losing access to its Moscow office and reader-donation system. Editor-in-chief Sergei Sokolov said Russian authorities and security services had forced the newsroom to stop working. The paper plans to publish a final issue. The closure follows years of restrictions that intensified after Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Authorities revoked the paper’s media licence, blocked its website and designated it a “foreign agent” in September 2026. This month, police searched Sokolov’s home, and investigative reporter Oleg Roldugin was arrested in a criminal case. Novaya Gazeta says the loss of its premises and funding left it unable to continue. Its separately operated sister publication, Novaya Gazeta Europe, will keep publishing from abroad. Founded in 1993, the newspaper became known for investigations into corruption and human-rights abuses. Six of its journalists and contributors were killed, including Anna Politkovskaya, who reported on the Chechen wars.

business.title: Italy
business.summary: Italian inflation accelerated to 5.4% in October from 4.2% in September, its highest level in more than three years, while the economy recorded no growth in the third quarter. Energy prices rose 31.4% year over year, and regulated energy tariffs climbed 59.5%; food and transport costs also increased. Finance Minister G
business.content: Italian inflation accelerated to 5.4% in October from 4.2% in September, its highest level in more than three years, while the economy recorded no growth in the third quarter. Energy prices rose 31.4% year over year, and regulated energy tariffs climbed 59.5%; food and transport costs also increased. Finance Minister Giancarlo Giorgetti blamed the jump on the war’s effect on energy commodities and said the government was raising the issue with international partners. October inflation was 4.9% in Spain, 3.4% in France and 2.8% in Germany, while eurozone output grew 0.4% in the third quarter. The European Central Bank kept its deposit rate at 2.5% on Thursday after discussing another increase; economists cited in the reporting said a December hike remained possible. Italy’s government is expected to present an energy-bill decree to the cabinet next week, with measures that could take effect on Jan. 1.

business.title: Hormuz tanker fires lift oil prices to six-month highs
business.summary: Oil prices closed Friday at six-month highs after Iran said four tankers caught fire when they struck mines in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s claims could not be independently verified; the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency separately reported attacks on vessels, including a tanker damaged by explosives attache
business.content: Oil prices closed Friday at six-month highs after Iran said four tankers caught fire when they struck mines in or near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran’s claims could not be independently verified; the UK Maritime Trade Operations agency separately reported attacks on vessels, including a tanker damaged by explosives attached to its hull. Brent settled at $117.64 a barrel and U.S. West Texas Intermediate at $104.12, with October gains of 13.6% and 15.2%, respectively. The strait normally carries about one-fifth of global oil consumption, but tanker movements have continued despite increased attacks. Qatari mediators returned to Tehran on Friday, and Iranian sources said another meeting could take place within a week in Doha or Istanbul. Reports also cited possible renewed U.S. strikes after the Nov. 3 midterm elections.
business.image_alt: Hormuz tanker fires lift oil prices to six-month highs

business.title: Bank of Japan doubles ETF sales as inflation outlook shifts
business.summary: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will more than double annual sales of exchange-traded funds (ETFs) from January 2027, accelerating its withdrawal from assets accumulated during years of monetary easing. The central bank said underlying inflation was generally consistent with its 2% target, which it adopted in 2013, and held it
business.content: The Bank of Japan (BOJ) will more than double annual sales of exchange-traded funds (ETFs) from January 2027, accelerating its withdrawal from assets accumulated during years of monetary easing. The central bank said underlying inflation was generally consistent with its 2% target, which it adopted in 2013, and held its policy rate at 1.25%. The bank said it must now guard against inflation rising above target, while Governor Kazuo Ueda cautioned that price stability had not yet been achieved sustainably. The decision to hold rates passed 8-1, and policymakers left open further increases depending on economic and price developments. Economists expect the next opportunity for a rate increase to come at the Dec. 17-18 meeting; the faster ETF sales schedule is set to begin in January.
business.image_alt: Bank of Japan doubles ETF sales as inflation outlook shifts

business.title: Teachers
business.summary: The American Federation of Teachers (AFT), a teachers’ union, sued the U.S. Department of Education on Oct. 30, seeking class-action status over delays and changes to payment credits affecting borrowers in Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), a federal program for government and nonprofit employees. The union allege
business.content: The American Federation of Teachers (AFT), a teachers’ union, sued the U.S. Department of Education on Oct. 30, seeking class-action status over delays and changes to payment credits affecting borrowers in Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF), a federal program for government and nonprofit employees. The union alleges the department has failed to process buyback requests and improperly removed previously credited payments, leaving borrowers continuing to pay loans they say should qualify for cancellation. The suit says 90,000 borrowers’ buyback applications remain unprocessed; a court filing cited by CNBC and WBUR put the pending total at 88,000 in the spring. PSLF, signed into law in 2007, cancels an eligible borrower’s remaining federal student-loan balance after 120 qualifying monthly payments, generally over 10 years. Education Department officials say they are correcting coding errors from the Biden administration that produced inaccurate payment counts, while the AFT says the delays violate borrowers’ rights.

business.title: Higher Halloween candy prices cut chocolate sales and squeeze Hershey
business.summary: U.S. candy prices are rising faster than food inflation, while shoppers are buying less chocolate for Halloween and choosing smaller packs and lower-cocoa sweets. Candy and chewing-gum prices rose 7.7% in the year through September; Wells Fargo estimates chocolate will cost about 8% more than it did last Halloween. Ove
business.content: U.S. candy prices are rising faster than food inflation, while shoppers are buying less chocolate for Halloween and choosing smaller packs and lower-cocoa sweets. Candy and chewing-gum prices rose 7.7% in the year through September; Wells Fargo estimates chocolate will cost about 8% more than it did last Halloween. Overall Halloween spending is still expected to reach a record $13.5 billion, but Hershey cut its 2026 organic sales-growth forecast to 3% from a previous range of 3% to 3.5%. Manufacturers face costs from cocoa bought at high prices, alongside higher costs for sugar, fuel, packaging and other ingredients; lower cocoa prices have not yet reached store shelves. NielsenIQ data show seasonal chocolate sales fell $33.1 million over nine weeks through Oct. 17, with milk chocolate accounting for most of the decline. Wells Fargo sector manager David Branch said consumers may not see price relief until early next year as cheaper cocoa moves through distribution.
business.image_alt: Higher Halloween candy prices cut chocolate sales and squeeze Hershey

business.title: Google says AI search is cutting ad revenue as investors scrutinize spending
business.summary: Google Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said the company’s AI Mode search feature is reducing advertising revenue from traditional search, as investors assess whether its AI spending can pay off without weakening its core business. His comments followed Alphabet’s earnings report, which missed analysts’ expecta
business.content: Google Chief Business Officer Philipp Schindler said the company’s AI Mode search feature is reducing advertising revenue from traditional search, as investors assess whether its AI spending can pay off without weakening its core business. His comments followed Alphabet’s earnings report, which missed analysts’ expectations and preceded a record one-day decline in the Google parent’s shares on Oct. 29. Alphabet’s third-quarter revenue rose 25% to $127.6 billion, but net income fell 25% to $26.17 billion. Free cash flow was negative $9.07 billion, marking a second consecutive quarter below zero. Capital spending reached $51.4 billion, largely to build AI infrastructure. Google Cloud revenue more than doubled to $30.71 billion. Alphabet finance chief Anat Ashkenazi said capital spending would increase significantly in 2027.
business.image_alt: Google says AI search is cutting ad revenue as investors scrutinize spending

business.title: Investors brace for US midterms as $40 trillion debt nears ceiling
business.summary: Investors are preparing for the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats favored to win the House and the Senate contest still close. The outcome could affect spending, tariffs and regulation during President Donald Trump’s final two years in office. National debt has exceeded $40 trillion, and the federal deficit
business.content: Investors are preparing for the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, with Democrats favored to win the House and the Senate contest still close. The outcome could affect spending, tariffs and regulation during President Donald Trump’s final two years in office. National debt has exceeded $40 trillion, and the federal deficit is expected to remain around 6% of gross domestic product; analysts see little prospect of a major fiscal reset under either party. The economy has continued to grow, but September inflation was 3.7%, above the Federal Reserve’s 2% target, while consumer sentiment is near the lowest level in the University of Michigan survey’s 74-year history. Spending on artificial intelligence (AI) has contributed more than one-fifth of U.S. economic growth in recent quarters. A Democratic win could increase congressional scrutiny of AI companies and constrain new spending, but Trump would retain veto power and executive authority. Investors are also watching the next federal funding deadline, Dec. 11, and a possible debt-ceiling confrontation in 2027.
business.image_alt: Investors brace for US midterms as $40 trillion debt nears ceiling

business.title: Canada and EU advance digital trade, mining finance and business links
business.summary: Canada and the European Union concluded negotiations on a digital-trade agreement and a competition pact at a Montreal summit on Oct. 30. They also agreed to support European Investment Bank financing for Canadian critical-mineral projects. The measures are intended to ease cross-border online sales and data flows, cur
business.content: Canada and the European Union concluded negotiations on a digital-trade agreement and a competition pact at a Montreal summit on Oct. 30. They also agreed to support European Investment Bank financing for Canadian critical-mineral projects. The measures are intended to ease cross-border online sales and data flows, curb anti-competitive practices and expand financing options for mining. The two sides also agreed to give Canadian businesses and researchers access to European supercomputers. The measures are part of the new Canada-EU Alliance for the Future, launched by Prime Minister Mark Carney, European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen and European Council President António Costa. They build on the existing Canada-EU free-trade pact, which has already removed most tariffs. The two sides are also exploring faster transfers through linked instant-payment systems and expanded Canadian participation in Europe’s Erasmus+ exchange program. The EU has no existing process or defined cost for the proposed associate relationship. Canadian officials said talks on trade irritants tied to EU carbon-border and anti-deforestation rules were close to a deal, but no agreement had been reached. Carney said ministers and European commissioners would meet in March, with negotiations on the proposed relationship targeted for completion in June 2027.
business.image_alt: Canada and EU advance digital trade, mining finance and business links

science.title: Google satellite runs AI model in orbit, testing space data centers
science.summary: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype has generated its first AI response in orbit, running the Gemma 4 AI model on board and sending a haiku back to Earth as the company tests computing hardware in space. Google launched the satellite aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 on Oct. 1, and it began computing after about three weeks o
science.content: Google’s Project Suncatcher prototype has generated its first AI response in orbit, running the Gemma 4 AI model on board and sending a haiku back to Earth as the company tests computing hardware in space. Google launched the satellite aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9 on Oct. 1, and it began computing after about three weeks of commissioning. It carries four Tensor Processing Units (TPUs) but can run only one at a time for roughly 20 minutes, with power generation capped at 1 kilowatt. Google’s next tests will measure how the chips withstand temperature extremes and radiation, which can damage data or hardware. If the tests succeed, Google plans to launch two interconnected satellites in 2027, with more power and optical links between them.
science.image_alt: Google satellite runs AI model in orbit, testing space data centers

science.title: Study says human-caused warming reversed early growth of next ice age
science.summary: A study published in Science says the Barnes Ice Cap on Canada’s Baffin Island began expanding about 2,000 years ago, then began retreating around 1960 as human-driven warming raised summer temperatures. The researchers interpret the earlier growth as the opening stage of a new glacial cycle that was reversed before a
science.content: A study published in Science says the Barnes Ice Cap on Canada’s Baffin Island began expanding about 2,000 years ago, then began retreating around 1960 as human-driven warming raised summer temperatures. The researchers interpret the earlier growth as the opening stage of a new glacial cycle that was reversed before a large ice sheet could develop. The interpretation is disputed: Climate physicist Andrey Ganopolski said the ice cap’s growth is insufficient to show that a new glacial cycle had begun. He cited modeling that puts the next ice age about 50,000 years away even without global warming.
science.image_alt: Study says human-caused warming reversed early growth of next ice age

science.title: Fly study links protein changes to memory; artery procedures show no cognitive gain
science.summary: A randomized trial of 291 people with severe carotid artery narrowing but no symptoms found that stenting or surgery did not improve cognition more than medication alone after one year. Separately, a six-year study of 10 million fruit flies found that increasing the protein Funes in older flies shifted amyloid proteins
science.content: A randomized trial of 291 people with severe carotid artery narrowing but no symptoms found that stenting or surgery did not improve cognition more than medication alone after one year. Separately, a six-year study of 10 million fruit flies found that increasing the protein Funes in older flies shifted amyloid proteins toward states seen in younger flies and improved memory. Whether similar protein changes occur in humans remains untested. Study leader Rubén Hervás received a €1 million Hong Kong government grant to investigate that question.
science.image_alt: Fly study links protein changes to memory; artery procedures show no cognitive gain

science.title: Uranium ditelluride shows coexisting superconducting states under pressure
science.summary: Cornell University researchers have shown that uranium ditelluride (UTe₂), a leading candidate for a topological superconductor, can host two distinct superconducting states at once under pressure. The finding does not prove that it is topological. The study, published Oct. 30 in Nature Physics, remapped the material’s
science.content: Cornell University researchers have shown that uranium ditelluride (UTe₂), a leading candidate for a topological superconductor, can host two distinct superconducting states at once under pressure. The finding does not prove that it is topological. The study, published Oct. 30 in Nature Physics, remapped the material’s behavior across pressure, temperature and magnetic field after earlier phase diagrams appeared to conflict with thermodynamics. The two states meet and compete in part of the phase diagram; as temperature falls, one can suppress the other’s superconductivity. The researchers said any quantum-computing application remains several steps away and that no one has yet convincingly demonstrated a topological superconductor.
science.image_alt: Uranium ditelluride shows coexisting superconducting states under pressure

science.title: US midterms could reshape climate policy and energy costs nationwide
science.summary: In the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, voters will choose all 435 House members and 35 senators in contests that could change congressional oversight of President Trump’s climate policies. Democrats could not reverse enacted rollbacks or pass legislation over a presidential veto. A House majority could give them leverag
science.content: In the Nov. 3 U.S. midterm elections, voters will choose all 435 House members and 35 senators in contests that could change congressional oversight of President Trump’s climate policies. Democrats could not reverse enacted rollbacks or pass legislation over a presidential veto. A House majority could give them leverage in budget negotiations and allow them to launch investigations; a Senate majority could give them leverage over confirmations. Democrats need a net gain of four Senate seats to take control. State elections and ballot measures could also affect climate policy. Supporters of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act want Congress to pass the energy permitting bill during the lame-duck session, before new members take office in January. The bill would make it easier to build energy infrastructure, but environmental advocates disagree over whether it would speed clean-energy projects or weaken protections while enabling more fossil-fuel development.
science.image_alt: US midterms could reshape climate policy and energy costs nationwide

science.title: Light-based methods build molecular structures and control motion and activity
science.summary: Researchers have reported three light-controlled chemistry techniques: a University of Hong Kong team used copper complexes and visible light to build three-dimensional, drug-like molecular structures; a Prague team used a light-switchable molecular motor to restrict a neighboring rotor’s motion; and another group deve
science.content: Researchers have reported three light-controlled chemistry techniques: a University of Hong Kong team used copper complexes and visible light to build three-dimensional, drug-like molecular structures; a Prague team used a light-switchable molecular motor to restrict a neighboring rotor’s motion; and another group developed red-light-activated cages for protein-degrading compounds. In the Hong Kong study, the method suppressed unwanted polymerization and worked with several classes of starting materials; researchers made products on a gram scale. The rotor study experimentally confirmed slower motion, but the roughly 300,000-fold rate reduction was calculated, not directly measured. The cage system, called RuPHOTACs, is designed to keep protein-degrading molecules inactive until low-energy red light activates them.
science.image_alt: Light-based methods build molecular structures and control motion and activity

science.title: Trial finds diet-and-exercise program led to diabetes remission in 54% of intervention participants
science.summary: An intensive diet-and-exercise program led to type 2 diabetes remission in 27 of 50 participants (54%) after 24 weeks, compared with two of 46 (about 4%) receiving usual care. The randomized trial enrolled 96 adults aged 18 to 45 with obesity in England and Canada. Eighty-six participants completed final assessments. F
science.content: An intensive diet-and-exercise program led to type 2 diabetes remission in 27 of 50 participants (54%) after 24 weeks, compared with two of 46 (about 4%) receiving usual care. The randomized trial enrolled 96 adults aged 18 to 45 with obesity in England and Canada. Eighty-six participants completed final assessments. For the first 12 weeks, the program prescribed 800 to 900 calories daily, supervised aerobic and resistance exercise twice weekly and one independent exercise session per week, followed by a weight-maintenance phase. Remission required a hemoglobin A1c (HbA1c) level below 6.5% and no glucose-lowering medication for at least 12 weeks. The researchers said longer-term studies are needed to determine whether the results persist in everyday settings.
science.image_alt: Trial finds diet-and-exercise program led to diabetes remission in 54% of intervention participants

science.title: Chile
science.summary: Astronomers using Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory identified 2026 ED138, an icy object beyond Neptune. It could become the solar system’s sixth recognized dwarf planet if further observations show it is large enough for its gravity to make it round. Current estimates put its diameter at 600 to 1,500 kilometers and it
science.content: Astronomers using Chile’s Vera C. Rubin Observatory identified 2026 ED138, an icy object beyond Neptune. It could become the solar system’s sixth recognized dwarf planet if further observations show it is large enough for its gravity to make it round. Current estimates put its diameter at 600 to 1,500 kilometers and its distance from the Sun at about 46 times Earth’s, farther out than Pluto’s average orbit. Astrophysicist Matthew Holman identified the object on Oct. 13 while searching Rubin observations for moving objects. Its apparent brightness suggests a large body, but the size estimate depends on how much sunlight its surface reflects. Astronomers need infrared observations to measure its physical size more precisely. Rubin recorded it repeatedly before the discovery, and researchers later found it in older telescope archives. The observatory’s decade-long survey will continue scanning the southern sky while astronomers pursue further measurements of ED138.

sports.title: South Africa set Australia 288-run chase in series-deciding Test
sports.summary: South Africa were bowled out for 387 on the fourth day of the third Test at Newlands on Friday, leaving Australia needing 288 runs to win the match and the series on Saturday, October 31. The teams are level at 1-1 after Australia won the first Test by 214 runs and South Africa replied with an innings-and-31-run victor
sports.content: South Africa were bowled out for 387 on the fourth day of the third Test at Newlands on Friday, leaving Australia needing 288 runs to win the match and the series on Saturday, October 31. The teams are level at 1-1 after Australia won the first Test by 214 runs and South Africa replied with an innings-and-31-run victory. South Africa batter Ryan Rickelton made 101 and Wiaan Mulder scored 115, sharing a 154-run sixth-wicket partnership that turned a 40-run lead into a 287-run advantage. South Africa had resumed at 140-4 after trailing by 100 in the first innings. Rickelton and Mulder batted for much of the day before a late collapse, with Mulder and Kagiso Rabada adding 36 for the last wicket. A win for either side on the final day would settle the series; a draw remains possible. South Africa need 10 wickets, while Australia face a wearing pitch offering more turn than earlier in the match.
sports.image_alt: South Africa set Australia 288-run chase in series-deciding Test

sports.title: Chelsea manager Alonso rules out January loan for teenager Estevao

sports.content: Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has ruled out a January loan for Brazilian winger Estêvão Willian, saying the 19-year-old remains part of his plans ahead of Saturday’s Premier League match against Manchester United. Estêvão has played 47 minutes in the league this season and was an unused substitute as Chelsea lost to Liverpool on penalties in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday. Alonso said Estêvão is adapting to the Premier League’s pace and learning what is required with and without the ball. He said the player’s training and attitude have been good. The winger is working to regain his place after a hamstring injury ended his previous season in April and ruled him out of the World Cup. Alonso said there had been no loan discussions and promised Estêvão playing time as the season progresses.

sports.content: Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James scored 20 points, including the go-ahead jumper and a late putback, to lead Philadelphia past the New York Knicks 98-93 on Friday in the teams’ opening game of the NBA Cup, the league’s in-season tournament. James finished with nine rebounds and eight assists, while guard Tyrese Maxey led Philadelphia with 27 points. Knicks guard Jalen Brunson put New York ahead 90-89 with a three-pointer with 1:32 left. James answered with a basket, and Philadelphia guard VJ Edgecombe added a three-pointer before James’ putback secured the win. Philadelphia improved to 5-1 with its second win over the reigning champions this season; the 76ers also beat New York on opening night. James, 41, recorded his first 20-point game in a Philadelphia uniform. The 76ers played without Jaylen Brown, who sat out with left knee soreness. NBA Cup group games continue through November and count toward regular-season standings. The quarterfinals are scheduled for Dec. 4-5, the semifinals for Dec. 8-9 and the final for Dec. 11 in Indianapolis. Philadelphia’s next game is Saturday at Charlotte.

sports.content: New England Patriots wide receiver A.J. Brown is questionable for Sunday’s game against the Miami Dolphins after a knee issue flared up while he was recovering from an ankle injury. Coach Mike Vrabel said the team would assess Brown on Saturday before deciding whether he can play. Brown missed four games after a high ankle sprain in the season opener and has played twice since returning from injured reserve. New England is already without wide receivers Romeo Doubs and Mack Hollins, both on injured reserve. The Patriots visit Miami on Nov. 1, with Brown’s status still pending.

sports.title: Brewers celebrate first World Series title before an estimated crowd of more than 750,000
sports.summary: Milwaukee celebrated the Brewers’ first World Series championship with a downtown parade and lakefront rally on Friday, Oct. 30. sports.content: Milwaukee celebrated the Brewers’ first World Series championship with a downtown parade and lakefront rally on Friday, Oct. 30. Police estimated more than 750,000 people attended, a turnout that could set Wisconsin’s record for a single-day event. Fans lined the route and filled Henry Maier Festival Park, where players displayed the trophy, greeted supporters and addressed the crowd. The parade paused at a mural of longtime broadcaster Bob Uecker, who died in 2025 after calling Brewers games for more than 50 years. The celebration followed Milwaukee’s five-game World Series victory over the Tampa Bay Rays, which secured the first title in franchise history. Team captain Christian Yelich said the players were excited to bring the trophy home and share it with fans. Jake Bauers, Brandon Woodruff and JoJo Romero are among Milwaukee’s key free agents as the club decides how to keep its championship roster together. The current collective bargaining agreement expires Dec. 1, and a possible lockout could disrupt baseball’s offseason.

sports.content: Everton omitted Manchester City loanee Jack Grealish from Thursday’s 3-1 Carabao Cup win over Newcastle United after the club said he had breached its disciplinary rules. Reports said he missed Monday’s training session without permission. Manager David Moyes backed the club’s decision but declined to explain the incident or say whether Grealish would return for Monday’s Premier League game against Newcastle. The result sent Everton into a quarter-final against League Two side Fleetwood Town in December. Moyes has described his squad as small. Grealish, 31, is back at Everton on loan for a second season after an injury-disrupted spell. His Manchester City contract runs through the end of this season. Everton face Newcastle again on Monday. Moyes has not confirmed whether Grealish will be available. Reports say the player has spoken with club officials and must avoid a repeat.

sports.content: Saúl “Canelo” Álvarez and WBC super-middleweight champion Christian Mbilli made weight Friday in Riyadh for their title fight scheduled for Saturday, Oct. 31. Álvarez weighed 167.6 pounds and Mbilli 167.8 pounds, both inside the 168-pound limit. The bout is the Mexican star’s first since Terence Crawford beat him in September 2025, ending his undisputed reign. Álvarez, 36, returns after a 13-month break that included elbow surgery to face Mbilli, 31, who is unbeaten in 30 professional fights and making his first defence as full WBC champion. A win would make Álvarez a world champion again; Mbilli is seeking the biggest victory of his career. The fight is proceeding despite missile and drone attacks in Saudi Arabia and travel disruption around Riyadh. Other sporting events in the kingdom have been cancelled or postponed. Mexican boxer Lindolfo Delgado withdrew from his scheduled vacant IBF light-welterweight title bout earlier in the week.

sports.title: Arsenal boss Arteta defends teen Dowman after three-game ban upheld

sports.content: Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta defended his angry reaction to 16-year-old Max Dowman’s dismissal after the Football Association rejected Arsenal’s appeal. He said the teenager must meet the same standards as senior players. Dowman was sent off in the 85th minute against fourth-tier Fleetwood Town for kicking out after a challenge by Harrison Neal; Arsenal then lost the Carabao Cup tie 5-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw. Arteta said he had warned Dowman before the match not to react to physical provocation and said it was the youngster’s second sending-off this month, following one for England’s under-19s. He said he spoke with Dowman on Thursday and that they had “no issues,” while arguing that protecting a 16-year-old must be balanced with fair expectations for the rest of the squad. The ban rules Dowman out of Arsenal’s Premier League games against Liverpool, Hull City and Newcastle. Arteta said he was disappointed by the appeal ruling and believed Dowman was fortunate to avoid a serious foot injury.
